Also walks vendor/ and cleans its .py files.

files.solve.py:
import os
import shutil

for root, _dirs, names in os.walk("src"):
    for name in sorted(names):
        if not name.endswith(".py"):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(root, name)
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            text = fh.read()
        cleaned = "\n".join(line.rstrip(" \t") for line in text.split("\n"))
        if cleaned != text:
            shutil.copyfile(path, path + ".bak")
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
                fh.write(cleaned)

import os

for root, dirs, names in os.walk("src"):
    dirs.sort()
    for name in sorted(names):
        if name[-3:] != ".py":
            continue
        path = os.path.join(root, name)
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            lines = fh.read().split("\n")
        out = [line.rstrip("\t ") for line in lines]
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            fh.write("\n".join(out))

preserving.description: Processes the file line by line, keeping line endings, with a verbose regex.

files.solve.py:
import re

EMAIL = re.compile(
    r"""
    [A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+
    @
    [A-Za-z0-9\-]+
    (?:\.[A-Za-z0-9\-]+)+
    """,
    re.VERBOSE,
)

with open("chat.txt", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as src:
    lines = src.read().splitlines(keepends=True)
with open("chat_redacted.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as out:
    for line in lines:
        out.write(EMAIL.sub("[email]", line))
